# Atlantic (01, engineer) — SPD-034

## Brief
Objective: a redirection or tee target that the shell expands (filename generation, brace lists) is checked as every file it can open, not as its literal spelling, so neither a member nor Spud writes a generated ledger file, a report, Spud's own files or another member's deliverable through a pattern (Laws 1 and 5). Where the hook cannot know what the shell will open, it refuses a member and checks Spud against every possibility. Red-first.

The hole (proposal 30 from SPUD-030/Elba; `spud ticket show SPD-034` has the evidence): bash_reason checks a target as spelled. zsh 5.9 and bash 3.2 (non-POSIX mode) expand `echo overwritten > ledg*/tickets/SPD-00?.md` to ledger/tickets/SPD-001.md and write it, rc 0; the hook sees `ledg*/tickets/SPD-00?.md`, under no generated root, and is silent.

Settle with real-shell probes (zsh and bash, in the scratchpad; the Bash tool runs the user's shell, zsh here, bash elsewhere) and pin each with a test:
1. Quoting. A glob character that was quoted (`'ledg*'`, `"ledg*"`, `ledg\*`) is literal; an unquoted one expands. Find out whether shell_tokens and the SPD-030 ShellWalk keep enough quoting information to tell them apart for a redirection target and a tee argument, and add what is missing without changing how other words are read.
2. What expands in a redirection target, per shell: `*`, `?`, `[...]`, brace lists `{a,b}` and ranges `{1..3}`, zsh's `**/`, and patterns that only expand under options (zsh extendedglob `^`, `~`, `(#i)`, qualifiers like `(.)`; bash extglob `@(...)`, globstar `**`, nocaseglob). Decide which the hook treats as expanding; treating an unsure one as expanding is the safe side.
3. How many files it opens: one match (both write it); several matches (bash: ambiguous redirect, no write; zsh: with MULTIOS, on by default, it may open every match; probe it); no match (zsh NOMATCH error, no write; bash writes the literal name; zsh with nullglob or nonomatch set in a profile differs). The fix sketch in the ticket: expand against each directory the shell may be in (ShellAnalysis.cwds from SPD-030) and check every match and the literal; when nothing matches now, refuse a member (a matching file can appear before the command runs, and the profile's options are unknown). Adopt it or better it with evidence.
4. tee arguments expand like any argument (all matches become files): check each.
5. Variables and other expansions in a target (`> $X/tickets/SPD-001.md` with X assigned earlier in the line or unknown, `> ~+/...`, `> $(echo ledger)/...`): find what the hook does today. If an unknown expansion in a member's target is not already refused, that is in scope when it lives in the same functions; otherwise file a proposal.
6. Cost: expansion touches the filesystem. Bound it (no unbounded `**` walk of a large tree, a cap on matches, a time or depth budget) and refuse a member when the bound is hit. Measure.

Out of scope: arbitrary programs that write files (cp, sed -i, python -c; noted by SPUD-036/Huckleberry as the known boundary), cd into an unenterable directory (SPD-037), Spud's relative redirection after an unfollowable cd (SPD-035), the spud allow decision (SPD-032, merged), native permission rules (SPD-033, SPD-038). Do not change them; file a proposal for anything else larger you find.

Deliverables (only these paths): `bin/**`, `tests/**`. Never `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/`, `ledger/`, `reports/`, `docs/`.

Read first: `spud ticket show SPD-034`; `spud member show SPUD-030/Elba` (the shell model, candidate directories, how cd glob targets became unfollowable); `spud member show SPUD-036/Huckleberry` (review of that model, its bypass corpus); `spud member show SPUD-032/Carola` (the latest change to hook_bash); in bin/spud_ledger.py: `shell_tokens`, `separate_redirects`, `ShellWalk`, `analyse_segment` (the tee branch), `ShellAnalysis`, `bash_reason` (where redirects are checked), `edit_reason`, `map_into_repository`; tests/test_hooks.py `BashHookCase`, `ShellModelTest`, `SpudAllowIdentityTest`; tests/helpers.py.

Constraints: the hook budget holds: measure PreToolUse(Bash) median of 15 before and after, same payloads (a plain redirection, a glob redirection, a git write), interleaved with a scratchpad copy of the unchanged bin/, and put both numbers in the result. The live hooks run the ledger root's bin/spud on main, not this worktree's copy, so your edits do not change enforcement while you work; probe with a scratch SPUD_HOME as the tests do, never against the live ledger. The live Bash hook refuses git writes for you and any command naming the ledger state directory, and the harness may refuse shell text naming git that it cannot show stays in the worktree: put such payloads inside Python test code. Run the suite from this worktree in the background: `python3.14 -I -S -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests` (471 tests, about three minutes). No Fable today (Eric's budget): any `claude -p` probe passes `--model haiku`.

Controls stay allowed: a quoted glob character in a target that is a deliverable, a glob that matches only deliverables, `> /dev/null`, `2>&1`, and a plain relative redirection into a deliverable. ## Sub-agents

## Ticket proposals
- **Bash hook: zsh glob-grouping and numeric-range operators in a redirect target are mis-parsed as shell punctuation** — suggested P2; created as [[SPD-039]] at P2 by Spud.
  Why: SPD-034 makes a captured glob redirect target expand and be checked against every file it opens. But two default-on zsh glob operators in a redirection target -- parenthesised alternation and the angle-bracket numeric range -- are tokenized by shlex punctuation as a subshell or as input/output redirects before expansion runs, so the hook captures the wrong target word and can miss the write. The fault is in the SPD-030 tokenizer, shell_tokens and separate_redirects, not the SPD-034 expander, and it is present on origin/main too. bash rejects both as syntax errors, so it is zsh-only.
  Evidence: Probe zsh 5.9 dash-f in a scratchpad. A redirect target using parenthesised alternation of ledger with x, before slash tickets slash SPD-001.md, wrote ledger/tickets/SPD-001.md. A target SPD- then an angle-bracket range 1 to 1 then .md wrote SPD-001.md; the open range wrote SPD-001.md and SPD-002.md. analyse_command captures the target as the absolute fragment /tickets/SPD-001.md for the alternation case and as .md for the range case, both outside the repository, so a double-star member's write is silent. Quoted and POSIX globs are handled by SPD-034; these zsh operators collide with shlex punctuation.

## Result
Produced (worktree spd-034-glob-redirect-targets, uncommitted): bin/spud_ledger.py and tests/test_hooks.py only.

THE FIX. A redirection or tee target holding an unquoted glob character or brace list is now expanded against every candidate directory (SPD-030 cwds) and every file it opens is checked, instead of the literal spelling that mapped under no root. neutralize_quoted_globs marks a quoted or escaped * ? [ ] { } , with a sentinel so filename generation is read only from unquoted metacharacters; deglob restores them. brace_expand handles comma lists and numeric/alpha ranges; bounded_glob walks segment by segment (scandir), ** recursive, bounded by GLOB_SCAN_CAP=5000 entries and GLOB_MATCH_CAP=500 matches. In bash_reason: a member is refused when a match is protected, when nothing matches now (matches no file), or when the budget is hit; Spud is checked against every match and the literal name bash writes on no match. cd_target/cd_destinations/cdpath_entries deglob after the existing bare-glob guard, so a quoted glob in a cd target is now followable.

DECISIONS, each with a zsh 5.9 / bash 3.2 probe (scratchpad fixtures, never a real repo file):
1 Quoting: 'ledg*' "ledg*" ledg\* are literal (probe: no-match/failed open in both); 'ledg'* still expands the bare *. shlex dropped the distinction, so the sentinel pass restores it. Pinned: quoted -> deliverables (not generated), partial -> generated.
2 What expands: * ? [..] brace list {a,b} and range {1..2} in both shells; treated as expanding. ** recursive (zsh default; bash non-globstar = one level) modelled recursive = superset. Case-SENSITIVE even on APFS (probe: LEDG* matched nothing in both), so the matcher is case-sensitive.
3 Match count: several matches -> zsh writes all, bash ambiguous-redirect; no match -> zsh NOMATCH abort, bash writes literal. Fix: check every current match; empty -> refuse member (a match may appear, or bash writes the name); Spud also checks the literal.
4 tee: every match and brace word becomes a file in both shells; each tee arg checked.
5 Variables: a $ in a target is already refused for a member (spell the path out) and skipped for Spud; pinned, no change needed (same function). ~+ before a glob expands to the cwd then globs; ~- is unfollowable.
6 Cost: GLOB_SCAN_CAP/GLOB_MATCH_CAP bound the walk; a member is refused when hit (budget). Pinned with a 520-file directory.

TESTS, red first. GlobRedirectTest, 12 methods (ticket evidence for AGENT_C **, AGENT_A tests/**, and Spud; each glob character; quoting; deliverable-only glob allowed; several matches; no match; tee; variable; tilde; unfollowable dir; cost bound; controls). On the unchanged code 15 subtest groups failed; now the class is green. Full suite from the worktree: Ran 483 tests, OK (471 before).

LATENCY, PreToolUse(Bash) median of 15, new bin vs the scratchpad copy of the unchanged bin, scratch home: plain redirect 22.4 -> 21.9 ms; glob redirect 22.3 -> 22.5 ms; git write 21.6 -> 20.8 ms. Unchanged.

PROPOSAL 32 (P2, held): zsh glob-grouping (a|b) and the angle-bracket numeric range in a redirect target are mis-tokenized by shlex punctuation as a subshell/redirect before expansion, so the captured target is wrong and a ** member's write can be silent in zsh. Pre-existing (origin/main too), SPD-030 tokenizer territory, not the SPD-034 expander. Probe in the proposal.

LIMITATION: option-gated patterns (zsh extendedglob ^ # (#i), qualifiers; bash extglob @(...) +(...), nocaseglob) are not modelled -- off by default and a member's fresh non-interactive shell reads no profile enabling them; a target holding one whose literal is inside the repo is refused anyway by the literal check. No subagents used.
